description: The corpus runs TWO Skein normalisations. AGENTS.md §7a (STRICT) mandates the Hecke-generator form L_+ - L_- = (q - 1/q) L_0, so the single-crossing amplitude is h_1 = q - 1/q. Seven content blocks across five chapters instead write the framed/Jones form q[L_+] - q^-1[L_-] = (q^(1/2) - q^(-1/2))[L_0], amplitude s = h_(1/2). They are NOT rescalings of one another (the L_+ : L_- weights are 1:1 against q:q^-1). The bridge is exact and already half-recorded in the corpus: h_1 = s(q^(1/2)+q^(-1/2)), hence h_1^2 = [2]_q^2 - 4 = s^2([2]_q + 2), ratio [2]_q + 2 = 4.0108995061 at the proton pin. That bridge factor is bar-EVEN, so bar-parity arguments are blind to the choice while every magnitude is not. prf:trace-ratio-observable takes the vertex amplitude in (J) while the weak-vertex trace is computed in H_3(q) with h = q - 1/q, i.e. (H) -- so one rate mixes the two. Under (H) throughout, qou-xql6's substitution factor is 32.2624 rather than 129.4051; the qou-ix74 scope-(a) negative survives either way. ANSWERS the open question of qou-q2l7: the {1/2,1/2} exponent pair is FORCED, by convention (J).

convention.anchor: proton pin (Q_50_DIGIT_STR); identities exact in q

consequence_for_the_beta_rate.qou_ix74_verdict: SURVIVES under either -- 32x and 129x are both far too large for a 10-17 % correction

answers: qou-q2l7's open remainder -- the {1/2,1/2} exponent pair of the decay coupling is FORCED by convention (J), not chosen ad hoc
scope: MEASUREMENT plus an AUTHOR DECISION not taken here. Measured: the two relations, their inequivalence, the exact bridge, the surface, the consequence. NOT decided: whether the rate is restated in (H) to match §7a, or §7a records (J) as the physics-sector convention. Both are coherent; either rewrites eight content blocks or a STRICT section. No identity here depends on the choice.

assertions.name: bridge_factor_is_the_bar_invariant_one
assertions.note: h_1 = s * (q^(1/2) + q^(-1/2)) exactly -- the corpus already states this factorisation in bar-involution-c5-algebraic-identities

assertions.name: h1_squared_is_two_q_squared_minus_four
assertions.note: h_1^2 = [2]_q^2 - 4 = s^2([2]_q + 2): the §7a amplitude squared is the (J) one times a bar-INVARIANT factor

assertions.name: the_two_relations_are_not_rescalings
assertions.note: (H) weights L_+ : L_- as 1 : 1; (J) as q : q^-1, ratio q^2. No overall factor relates them, so these are different skein presentations rather than one relation written twice

assertions.name: bridge_factor_is_bar_invariant
assertions.note: q^(1/2)+q^(-1/2) is bar-EVEN while s is bar-ODD, so bar-parity arguments cannot see the convention choice -- only magnitudes can

assertions.name: substitution_factor_moves_but_verdict_does_not
assertions.note: |W|^2/h_1^2 = 32.2624 against |W|^2/s^2 = 129.4051. Both are far too large to be the 10-17 % correction of qou-ix74, so that scope-(a) negative survives under either convention

assertions.name: convention_J_surface_is_multi_chapter_not_one_block
assertions.note: 8 of 8 listed blocks still carry the sqrt-q amplitude, across five chapters -- a corpus-wide split, not a single-block slip
